text:
alex_cs: heads up — Suncrest is seeing a sudden p99 jump for embeddings API on us-east-1 since ~09:00 UTC. p95 went from ~120ms to ~900ms, p99 ~3s. They called out a recent tenant move to a new shard. Can we triage?

maria_support: noted, pinging eng-sre and infra. Do we have tenant_id and a repro request from them?

alex_cs: tenant_id=tenant_suncrest_42. They sent a sample request and timestamps:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -d '{"model":"embed-lite-3","input":["search term 1","search term 2"]}'
```
Response times attached in their logs: ~2.8s for ~10% of calls since 09:00.

jin_sre: thanks. I'm going to pull per-tenant tail metrics and the shard queue length. Running quick aggregation now.

jin_sre: quick dump (truncated):
```
> shard=us-east-1-azb
> tenant: tenant_suncrest_42 p50=95ms p95=870ms p99=3012ms req/s=4.1
> shard queue depth: global=23 per-tenant=6 (threshold warn=10)
> hotkeys: none; kernel async wait spikes at 09:02-09:18
```

leo_infra: queue depth per-tenant=6 suggests contention but not full saturation. Could be noisy neighbor on same GPU group. We can try: 1) temporary reservation (burst pool) 2) priority lane allowlist so their requests bypass some batching heuristics 3) pin to a smaller quantized variant for short-term. Which do you prefer for quick mitigation?

sara_eng: for quickest impact, priority lane allowlist + small reservation tends to reduce p99 fastest. Pinning to smaller model helps cost and latency but may affect quality — confirm with CS.

maria_support: talked to Suncrest ops; they accept temporary allowlist + reservation for 30m while we investigate. Please apply and I'll tell them.

jin_sre: creating reservation and adding tenant to priority lane now.

deploy-bot: reservation created: res-3061234567-suncrest-burst (30m). priority-lane: added tenant_suncrest_42 -> policy=priority-burst-temp.

jin_sre: applied priority-lane, bumped token budget for this tenant in the shard, and set autoscale bias +20% for res. Monitoring raw RTs and kernel wait.

jin_sre: 15m after mitigation:
```
> tenant_suncrest_42 p50=88ms p95=210ms p99=412ms req/s=4.2
> shard queue depth: global=12 per-tenant=2
> kernel async wait returned to baseline
```

maria_support: relayed to Suncrest — they confirm user-facing latency improved, no errors reported. They asked for root cause once we have it.

leo_infra: next steps: 1) snapshot scheduling logs for 08:30-09:30 across the shard, 2) check if a high-throughput tenant was colocated (we saw one transient spike from tenant_vivara_09 at 09:05 producing 250 rps for 2m), 3) audit autoscaler decisions. I'll take #1 and #2.

sara_eng: I'll run model variant perf diff for embed-lite-3 vs embed-lite-3-quant to see how fallback would affect quality; will link evals.

jin_sre: marking this thread as mitigated for now. Please file follow-up investigation ticket with logs and attach to the customer incident: INC-30612. I'll keep monitoring for 1h and will escalate if it recurs.

maria_support: thanks all — closing customer-facing loop. Suncrest asked whether we can make the allowlist permanent for their SLA; they'll open a formal request.

alex_cs: noted. adding summary to the ticket: temporary priority-lane + 30m reservation reduced p99 from ~3s to ~412ms; probable noisy neighbor (tenant_vivara_09) spike at 09:05. Follow-ups: colocated-tenant audit, autoscaler review, model-variant evals.

jin_sre: follow-up update (30m later): metrics stable, no recurrence. Leaving reservation to expire as scheduled. :thumbsup:

maria_support: closing thread, will track INC-30612 for RCA and CS request for permanent SLA change.
